title: Scalable; generalizable and uncertainty-aware integration of spatial multiomics across diverse modalities and platforms with SCIGMA.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: no PMCID, no full text, no accessions, no NCBI links. Downloaded both files of the Zenodo record 19822850 (CC-BY-4.0): SCIGMA.zip (690 KB) and SCIGMA_analyses.zip (112 KB). Listed both: they hold only code, notebooks, R scripts and a tutorial, with no data tables. Read the data-download notebooks: every dataset is reused from elsewhere (SpatialGlue Zenodo 10362607 for SPOTS mouse spleen and spatial ATAC-seq mouse brain, GEO GSE263333 for Spatial-Mux-Seq, 10x Genomics public pages for Xenium Prime and Visium HD). Read run_metrics.py: the benchmark scores clustering reproducibility (pairwise ARI, adjusted Rand index, and Jaccard similarity between runs), not agreement with a measured label.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The 19 datasets, 8 modalities, 10 tissues, 9 platforms and the >1 million spatial locations come from the abstract only. I did not see the paper's main text or which datasets carry manual spatial-domain annotations.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo record is open (CC-BY-4.0) but holds code only; the underlying datasets are public on other Zenodo records, GEO and 10x Genomics pages. Checked in files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No prediction target exists. SCIGMA is unsupervised integration (joint embedding plus clustering into spatial domains); its own metrics script scores run-to-run reproducibility, not a measured label. Any 'ground truth' would be hand-drawn domain annotations for a few tissue sections, which you'd have to build or collect from other papers. Checked in files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs (count matrices per modality plus spot coordinates) are public, but in 7+ different formats across repositories. Not opened.

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable without a label; the inputs are raw counts or intensities per modality.

a5_enough_rows.note: Spots number in the millions, but the independent unit is the tissue section: 19 datasets (abstract), with only a handful annotated. That is far below 400 labelled units.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Unknown; Visium HD and Xenium Prime datasets run to several GB each
a6_fits_laptop.note: The README says the authors used a 24 GB GPU with 100 GB RAM, or 24 CPUs with up to 400 GB RAM. Read in files (README).

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checked: no table of counts was deposited to compare against.

a8_label_provenance.note: Spatial domains, the paper's main output, are clusters computed from the same features the model integrates (circular). Manual annotations, where they exist, are expert judgement, not a measurement.

existing_models.name: SCIGMA (this paper), a contrastive graph neural network for integrating spatial multiomics
existing_models.score_and_split: Abstract claims it beats other methods on spatial domain detection, feature reconstruction and reproducibility on 'benchmarkable' datasets; I saw no numbers.

existing_models.name: SpatialGlue, a dual-attention graph neural network for spatial multiomics (Long et al.)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; used as a benchmark in SCIGMA's scripts.

existing_models.name: MultiGATE, a two-level graph attention autoencoder (Nature Communications 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search snippet: AUROC 0.703 for regulatory inference vs Cicero 0.530; best combined ICC among five methods.

existing_models.name: PRAGA, a prototype-aware graph aggregation method (GitHub Xubin-s-Lab/PRAGA)

backbone.name: None fits well: scGPT or Geneformer, single-cell models, cover only the RNA modality
backbone.licence: Code licence file present in SCIGMA.zip (34 KB, likely GPL); Zenodo record CC-BY-4.0

honest_claim_h3: No supervised claim is possible: the project would only be another unsupervised integration method, judged by clustering agreement on a few annotated tissue sections.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use paired spatial measurements (RNA, chromatin, protein) from tissue sections to predict which tissue region each spot belongs to.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-spot molecular profiles plus spot coordinates from about 19 public tissue sections (count from abstract); the number of annotated sections is unknown.
plain_idea.predict: A tissue-region label per spot, which exists only as hand-drawn expert annotations on a few sections, or as clusters computed from the same data.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Better tissue-region maps help spatial biologists, but a crowded field of unsupervised methods already does this, and the 'truth' is opinion, not measurement.

more_or_better_data.why: SCIGMA generates no new data; it reuses the same public datasets (SpatialGlue's Zenodo 10362607, GEO GSE263333, 10x demo data) that SpatialGlue and other methods use.

confidence_score.why: SCIGMA already reports per-spot uncertainty, its headline feature.

models_beatable.why: SCIGMA is a 2026 Nature Genetics model tested on 19 datasets; without a measured label there is no clear metric on which to beat it.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No labelled quantity exists, so no added dataset can make better predictions certain.

ml_idea: Considered: supervised spatial-domain prediction or a re-benchmark of integration methods. Dropped because there is no measured label, the unit is the tissue section (about 19), and the work needs a GPU.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; the authors' README states a 24 GB GPU or up to 400 GB RAM.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the tissue sections with independent manual domain annotations; already effectively failed (SCIGMA's own metric script uses run-to-run ARI, not ground truth).

verdict_reason: A method paper with no new data: the Zenodo deposit is code only, the task is unsupervised with no measured label (A2/A8), there are about 19 tissue sections as independent units (A5), it needs a GPU (A6), and the field is crowded (SpatialGlue, MultiGATE, PRAGA).
